newsitem.title: FRANCE: France deplores Jerusalem bloodshed, raps Israel.
newsitem.headline: France deplores Jerusalem bloodshed, raps Israel.

text.p: France deplored a new outburst of violence in the Old City of Jerusalem on Friday, urged all sides to avoid disproportionate force and the use of firearms and told Israel not to obstruct Palestinian ambulances.

Israeli security forces killed at least three Arabs and wounded 50 when they stormed Jerusalem's al-Aqsa mosque complex to disperse Palestinian stone-throwers, protesting against the opening of an ancient tunnel under the Old City, witnesses said.

A French foreign ministry statement said: "The French authorities deplore the new and grave incidents which erupted this morning in the city of Jerusalem...It calls on all parties to show the greatest restraint and refrain from resorting to disproportionate responses, especially the use of firearms."
"The French authorities appeal to the Israeli authorities to allow ambulances and rescue vehicles free and unhindered access to hospitals," it said.
France dispatched 2.5 tonnes of medicine and medical equipment to the Palestinian autonomous territories on Friday.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux said Paris was seeking joint aid from the European Union, and the French embassy had also urged Israeli authorities to take steps to defuse tension.
The embassy had asked Israeli authorities to allow ambulances to drive to Makassed hospital in Jerusalem despite the closure of Palestinians territories.
On Thursday, France asked Israel to close down the tunnel whose opening near Jerusalem's Temple Mount triggered the worst wave of violence since the 1993 Israel-PLO peace accords.
Israel's cabinet secretary, Danny Naveh, said police had closed the tunnel for security reasons and only temporarily.
